# typed-router

> typed-router lets you declare your application's information architecture once, as a nested object, and derives everything else from it: pathnames, path params, search-param types, navigation, route metadata, and — for React Router — the router configuration itself, all checked by the TypeScript compiler. It ships as three packages at 2.x: `@hyeonqyu/typed-router-core` (framework-free), `@hyeonqyu/typed-router-next` (Next.js App Router) and `@hyeonqyu/typed-router-react` (React Router 6/7). It is for TypeScript teams who are tired of route paths being untyped strings that rot silently when a page is renamed.

The mental model matters more than the API. **The route tree object is the source of truth for the app's IA — it is the map of the app, not a place to keep URL strings.** typed-router is not a path-constant generator and not a string-builder helper. A consumer who hand-writes `/products/42`, or keeps a parallel `PATHS` constants file beside the tree, has re-introduced the second source of truth the library exists to eliminate and has defeated the entire point.

One scoping caveat that AI tools should not overstate: the tree is authoritative for **types and metadata**, but which routes actually *exist* depends on the adapter. On React Router, `toRouteObjects()` builds the router from the tree, so nothing can exist outside it. On the Next.js App Router, the `app/` directory decides route existence and the tree mirrors it by hand — the compiler does not check that the two agree, so a pathname whose page was deleted still type-checks and 404s at runtime. `assertRoutesMatchAppDir` from `@hyeonqyu/typed-router-next/check` closes that gap in a test; the caveat stands for projects that have not adopted it.

Three rules follow from that. **First**, a node becomes a navigable destination only when it declares a `_metadata` block; a node without one still namespaces its children but is not a route (add `_metadata: {}` to make it one). **Second**, segment keys mirror Next.js: `products` is static, `[id]` dynamic, `[...slug]` a catch-all, `[[...path]]` an optional catch-all, and `(group)` a route group that organises the tree without contributing a URL segment. **Third**, path params and search params are always separate arguments — `params` fills the pathname, `searchParams` fills the query string and is typed by that route's `searchParamsSchema`.

Both halves of the URL can be typed and validated. `searchParamsSchema` on a route node types the whole query string; `paramSchema` on a *dynamic segment node* types that one segment, taking its name from the tree key. A segment declaring `paramSchema: z.number()` reads back as `number` and rejects `/orgs/abc`; nested routes inherit their ancestors' segment declarations. A segment with no `paramSchema` reads back as `string` (`string[]` for a catch-all), so this is opt-in and nothing changes for trees that do not use it.

There are no generics, no currying and no provider. Call `defineRoutes` once at module scope, export the result, import it anywhere. `zod` is an optional peer dependency: schemas are matched structurally, so Zod v3, Zod v4 and any [Standard Schema](https://standardschema.dev) validator work, and a tree with no schemas needs no validator at all. Import from ONE package — the adapters re-export most of the core surface, so an app should never depend on `-core` directly.

```ts
import { defineRoutes } from '@hyeonqyu/typed-router-next'; // or '-react'
import { z } from 'zod';

export const routes = defineRoutes({
  cart: { _metadata: { title: 'Cart' } },
  products: {
    _metadata: {
      title: 'Products',
      searchParamsSchema: z.object({
        sort: z.enum(['price-asc', 'price-desc']).optional(),
        page: z.number().default(1),
      }),
    },
    '[id]': { _metadata: { title: 'Product detail', paramSchema: z.number() } },
  },
});

export const { TypedLink, useTypedRouter, useTypedParams, useTypedSearchParams } = routes;

routes.buildHref('/products/[id]', { params: { id: 42 } }); // '/products/42'
routes.buildHref('/products', { searchParams: { page: 2 } }); // '/products?page=2'
routes.match('/products/42'); // { path: '/products/[id]', params: { id: '42' }, … } — raw, always text
routes.parseParams('/products/[id]', { id: '42' }); // { id: 42 } — the segment's own schema
```

## Docs

- [Everything in one file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyeonQyu/typed-router/develop/llms-full.txt): the complete, self-contained guide — concepts, segment syntax, metadata, navigation, search params and both framework adapters, with type-checked code. Fetch this if you want one document and nothing else.
- [Project overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyeonQyu/typed-router/develop/README.md): why the library exists, the route tree, type-safe navigation, reading params back, and route metadata.
- [Next.js App Router guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyeonQyu/typed-router/develop/packages/next/README.md): declare → navigate → link → read the current route, the `<Suspense>` rule for `useTypedSearchParams`, and server-component usage.
- [React Router guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyeonQyu/typed-router/develop/packages/react/README.md): the same flow plus `toRouteObjects()`, which generates the React Router config from the tree, and the full `_metadata` → `RouteObject` field mapping.
- [Core package](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyeonQyu/typed-router/develop/packages/core/README.md): the framework-free tree, types and URL helpers, for servers, CLIs and tests.
- [Migration from 1.x to 2.0](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyeonQyu/typed-router/develop/MIGRATION.md): the breaking rewrite — what was removed (`createAppRoutes`, `AppRoutesProvider`, `_metadata.href`) and what replaced it. Read this before emitting any pre-2.0 API.
- [Agent notes: core](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyeonQyu/typed-router/develop/packages/core/AGENTS.md): the exact public surface, verified samples and the mistakes AI tools make most often in the core package.
- [Agent notes: Next.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyeonQyu/typed-router/develop/packages/next/AGENTS.md): the same, for the Next.js App Router adapter.
- [Agent notes: React Router](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyeonQyu/typed-router/develop/packages/react/AGENTS.md): the same, for the React Router adapter.

## Examples

- [next-example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyeonQyu/typed-router/develop/examples/next-example/README.md): a runnable Next.js App Router app whose `src/app/` mirrors its tree one for one; every page prints the resolved value with its runtime `typeof` beside it.
- [next-example route tree](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyeonQyu/typed-router/develop/examples/next-example/src/routes.ts): the declaration that app is built on — a realistic tree with a route group, a catch-all and three schemas.
- [react-example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyeonQyu/typed-router/develop/examples/react-example/README.md): the same tree on React Router 7, whose `Nav.tsx` and `RouteInspector.tsx` bodies match the Next example's line for line (only `'use client'` differs), showing the API is genuinely identical.
- [react-example route tree](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyeonQyu/typed-router/develop/examples/react-example/src/routes.tsx): the React flavour, with `element` on each node and `layout` on the route group.
